note: The frozen shape of a recorded decision. Both platforms write this, and a statistics screen reads only this. Changing or removing a field raises eventSchemaVersion and requires a migration on every platform that already stores events.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable identifier for this event, unique on the device.

fields.name: restrictedAppRef
fields.description: The catalog entry identifier the event belongs to. Never a package name or a bundle identifier, so an event survives a platform renaming the application underneath it.

fields.name: occurredAt
fields.description: When the block was presented, as an absolute instant with an explicit offset.

fields.name: zone
fields.description: The device zone at that moment, so a later reader can group events into the days the user actually experienced, even after the user has travelled.

fields.name: primaryReason
fields.description: The single reason shown to the user, chosen by the priority order.

fields.name: allReasons
fields.description: Every reason that applied, in priority order, always including primaryReason. This is what keeps the record honest when several rules fire at once.

fields.name: userAction
fields.description: What the user decided. DISMISSED_BY_SYSTEM is for a block removed without a decision, such as a watchdog timeout or the foreground moving elsewhere. UNKNOWN is for a block whose outcome was lost, and it must never be counted as either a refusal or a bypass.

fields.name: bypassDurationMinutes
fields.description: Present only when userAction is BYPASSED. Records the duration actually granted, which may differ from the duration the product prefers when a platform cannot honour the shorter one.

fields.name: eventSchemaVersion
fields.description: The version of this contract the event was written under.

rules: primaryReason is always present in allReasons.
allReasons is ordered by the priority order in rule-priority-cases.json.
bypassDurationMinutes is non-null if and only if userAction is BYPASSED.
An event is written for every block that was presented, including those the system dismissed.
UNKNOWN is never counted as a refusal or as a bypass in any statistic.
A bypass that was granted is a legitimate outcome and is never presented as a failure.

changesFromTheSpecification.reason: docs/PRODUCT.md requires that when several rules apply the user sees one clear reason while all reasons are preserved in the event record. A single field cannot carry both. docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md section 2 is updated to match.
